We will investigate the connection between the determinant of a matrix and its invertibility using Gaussian elimination.

Consider the two upper triangular matrices $$ U_1 = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 4 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ \end{array}\right],~~~ U_2 = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 4 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$ Remembering [proposition-triangular-invertibility], which of the matrices $U_1$ and $U_2$ are invertible? What are the determinants $\det(U_1)$ and $\det(U_2)$?

Explain why an upper triangular matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is not zero.

Let's now consider the matrix $$ A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp -6 \\ 3 \amp -1 \amp 10 \\ \end{array}\right] $$ and begin the Gaussian elimination process with a row replacement operation $$ A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp -6 \\ 3 \amp -1 \amp 10 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 3 \amp -1 \amp 10 \\ \end{array}\right] = A_1 $$ . What is the relationship between $\det(A)$ and $\det(A_1)$?

Next we perform another row replacement operation: $$ A_1= \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 3 \amp -1 \amp 10 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 4 \\ \end{array}\right] = A_2 $$ . What is the relationship between $\det(A)$ and $\det(A_2)$?

Finally, we perform an interchange: $$ A_2 = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 4 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 4 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ \end{array}\right] = U $$ to arrive at an upper triangular matrix $U$. What is the relationship between $\det(A)$ and $\det(U)$?

Since $U$ is upper triangular, we can compute its determinant, which allows us to find $\det(A)$. What is $\det(A)$? Is $A$ invertible?

Now consider the matrix $$ A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp -1 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp -2 \\ 2 \amp 1 \amp 3 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$ Perform a sequence of row operations to find an upper triangular matrix $U$ that is row equivalent to $A$. Use this to determine $\det(A)$ and whether $A$ is invertible.

Suppose we apply a sequence of row operations on a matrix $A$ to obtain $A'$. Explain why $\det(A) \neq 0$ if and only if $\det(A') \neq 0$.

Explain why an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $\det(A) \neq 0$.
